language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, I'm Erik. I live in Norway. I love to go on adventures and explore the land and sea. I like to look at all the different animals, and observe what makes animals similar and different.

My friends from all over the world sent me pictures of animals from where they live. I like to see how animals have adapted to living in different places. For example, living outside in cold winters would be hard!
I've noticed that arctic foxe's fur is brown in the summer and changes to white during the winter. That way they are always camouflaged!
Some of my friends are planning a big sailing adventure. They are thinking about taking some animals with them to far away places. I'm worried some animals might not survive in another habitat.
If you help me fill in some missing gaps in my Explorer's Notebook, we can understand whether some animals may have trouble surviving somewhere else.
Let's explore with Erik – I think we can help him out!

I’ve noticed some patterns across the pictures and descriptions of animals I have collected from my explorations and from my friends around the world.

These patterns hold useful clues as to what kind of habitat an animal lives in. You see, animals adapt to their habitat. A clue might be the webbed feet of a duck: that tells you it lives in a water environment! Can you organize the other clues for me?

The appearance of an animal can give us a lot of clues about what it likes to eat. For example, have you ever noticed how some birds have really different beaks?

I love the big colourful beak of the Puffin! My notes about birds have got a
bit scrambled - can you help me figure out what food each bird eats?

helperSimple.text: Look closely at each bird – look at the size and shape of their beaks, how big their wings are, and their claws for clues. Match each bird with the correct diet notes.

Animals have multiple adaptations for different aspects of their survival.
It's important to understand all of the adaptations an animal has for survival, especially if we are considering changing an animal's habitat.

helperSimple.text: Help Erik complete his Explorer's Notebook by matching each adaptation to the best explanation.
